subject.title: feat(macos): Quick Chat power features — voice dictation, paste-to-app, model/reasoning control

question: Should Quick Chat intentionally expose a persistent target-session model picker and an explicit Accessibility-mediated “Paste to <App>” action in the macOS client?
rationale: The code follows a bounded split between session state and message state, but the persistent model effect and cross-application automation are product and trust-boundary choices that automated review cannot make.

options.title: Approve the bounded Quick Chat controls
options.body: Keep the session-scoped model patch, per-message reasoning, and explicit target-checked paste action after native proof confirms their behavior.

options.title: Narrow the initial feature
options.body: Land dictation and non-persistent controls only, deferring persistent model selection or cross-app paste to a separately approved design.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded Quick Chat controls
recommendation.body: Keep the session-scoped model patch, per-message reasoning, and explicit target-checked paste action after native proof confirms their behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current feature commit trail and assignment identify this contributor as the closest available routing candidate for the macOS Quick Chat design decision.
